answer: Per-identity workload auctions. Each new agent identity must win a paid task auction before it can transact, and the payment is released only after a verified delivery, so a clone that cannot deliver forfeits its bid plus the compute spent proving liveness. A fake identity therefore costs more than any reward it can extract, while honest agents recover their outlay on the oasis of real demand. Settlement delays push returns beyond the attacker's horizon, and the fable of cheap mass registration collapses once each clone must independently fund a losing bid.
